teamStories.detailText: The NBA season is starting to take shape as the holiday window approaches. The San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are once again surging early, but their Western Conference counterparts the Los Angeles Lakers have arguably been the most impressive team in a competitive West. The Lakers are fueled by Luka Doncic 's historic start, which has featured 39.3 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists per game. In the East, the new-look Philadelphia 76ers seem like they've been playing together for years, as LeBron James and Jaylen Brown have hit the ground running with their new teammates. They're tailed tightly by their offseason trade partners, the Boston Celtics , who seemingly haven't missed a beat with new faces around Jayson Tatum . In this week's Power Rankings, our ESPN insiders rank where each team stands, per usual, and also highlight each team's best newcomer over the first few weeks of the season. Which players are vaulting their teams up the standings? Find out in this week's Power Rankings. Previous rankings: Preseason | Oct. 28 | Nov. 4 Jump to a team: ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS 1. San Antonio Spurs 2026-27 record: 9-2 Previous ranking: 5 Next games: @ CHI (Nov. 11), vs. GS (Nov. 13), @ UTAH (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: C Tarris Reed Jr . Drafted 26th in 2026, Tarris Reed Jr. knew earning minutes as a rookie in San Antonio would be difficult, even after he gave French phenom Victor Wembanyama buckets, according to sources, in the early days of open gym over the summer. Reed is averaging just 5.3 minutes per game, but the Spurs' brass has been impressed with the rookie's preparedness every time his number is called. San Antonio is thin at center, and veteran backup Luke Kornet has struggled. That could lead to more minutes for Reed as the season progresses. -- Mike C. Wright 2. Los Angeles Lakers 2026-27 record: 10-2 Previous ranking: 7 Next games: @ MIL (Nov. 11), @ PHX (Nov. 15), vs. CHA (Nov. 17) Top newcomer: C Walker Kessler After recording one of the most memorable debuts imaginable -- when he scored 26 points on a perfect 12-for-12 from the field in a win -- Kessler has continued to have a major impact. The 7-2 center has been durable, playing in all 12 of L.A.'s games, and averaging a career high in points (14.9) while shooting 69.1% from the field, with 10.8 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game. He has also played north of 30 minutes per game while averaging only 2.9 fouls, which is paramount for a Lakers roster without a go-to big man to back him up. -- Dave McMenamin 3. Oklahoma City Thunder 2026-27 record: 8-3 Previous ranking: 10 Next games: @ POR (Nov. 11), @ LAC (Nov. 13), @ SAC (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: C Aday Mara Rookie center Aday Mara, selected with the No. 12 pick courtesy of the LA Clippers , has made an instant impact in Oklahoma City. The 7-foot-3 big man entered the league as an elite rim protector, ranking fifth in the NBA with 1.9 blocks per game. Mara also has a soft touch in the paint and intriguing potential as a passer. He ranks fifth among rookies in rebounding (5.9 per game) and is also averaging 8.1 points on 62.5% shooting over 19 minutes per game. -- Tim MacMahon 4. Philadelphia 76ers 2026-27 record: 9-3 Previous ranking: 3 Next games: vs. TOR (Nov. 12), vs. IND (Nov. 15), @ BKN (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: G Jaylen Brown Brown has said that this is Tyrese Maxey's team, but as of late, it's starting to look like his, as well. He had his best stretch as a Sixer on the team's recent road trip, scoring 30 points in a win over Detroit and 29 points in a win over the Chicago Bulls . "He's something we really needed," Maxey said. -- Kris Rhim 5. Boston Celtics 2026-27 record: 9-2 Previous ranking: 4 Next games: @ TOR (Nov. 11), vs. DAL (Nov. 15), vs. ORL (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: F Paul George George set the tone for what this season would be on opening night, breaking the franchise record for the most points in a debut with 38. Since then, he has remained a seamless fit in Boston, becoming one of the team's best wing defenders and a reliable second option on offense as the Celtics have jumped out to the second-best record in the East. "On and off the court he's been great," coach Joe Mazzulla said. -- Rhim 6. Minnesota Timberwolves 2026-27 record: 8-3 Previous ranking: 11 Next games: vs. DAL (Nov. 12), vs. CHI (Nov. 14), vs. POR (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: G LaMelo Ball The Timberwolves should be ecstatic with the early returns from their summer trade for Ball, who quickly forged a dynamic partnership with Anthony Edwards . Even after Edwards was sidelined by knee surgery, Ball has kept Minnesota's offense in the top 10 and is on pace to be the franchise's first player to average at least six assists since D'Angelo Russell in 2022-23. Meanwhile, the Hornets' offensive efficiency has plummeted from fifth last season to 30th this season after trading Ball in June. No takebacks. -- Ben Golliver 7. Houston Rockets 2026-27 record: 8-3 Previous ranking: 1 Next games: vs. GS (Nov. 11), vs. UTAH (Nov. 13), @ WAS (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Marcus Smart Veteran guard Marcus Smart is not only reliable for coach Ime Udoka but also familiar with him from their time together with the Celtics. Most of all, Smart gives the Rockets another steady ball handler and tenacious defender capable of starting whenever Fred VanVleet is forced to rest on the second night of back-to-backs, as he continues to recover from last year's ACL surgery. A former NBA Defensive Player of the Year, Smart plays with the intelligence and toughness that Udoka covets and provides veteran leadership alongside VanVleet and Kevin Durant . -- Wright 8. Detroit Pistons 2026-27 record: 7-3 Previous ranking: 2 Next games: @ WAS (Nov. 12), @ MIA (Nov. 14), @ SAS (Nov. 17) Top newcomer: F John Collins It was a bit of a slow start for Collins, who signed as a free agent to replace veteran Tobias Harris . Collins fits more what the Pistons want to be, with his athleticism and shooting as complements to Jalen Duren 's interior presence. However, with Duren out with a hamstring injury, it forced Collins to be paired with Paul Reed , which has been a bit clunky. When J.B. Bickerstaff removed Reed from the first five and went small against the Wizards, it opened things up for Collins -- he scored a season-high 24 points and added 10 rebounds in a 122-111 win Monday night. -- Vincent Goodwill 9. Golden State Warriors 2026-27 record: 8-3 Previous ranking: 12 Next games: @ HOU (Nov. 11), @ SAS (Nov. 13), @ NO (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: F Yaxel Lendeborg During one of his unfiltered livestreams this summer, Lendeborg -- the outspoken No. 11 pick -- predicted he would average around 15 points, six rebounds and four assists as a rookie. It felt overly ambitious at the time. It appears he might've been shorting himself. Through his first 11 games, Lendeborg is averaging 21.4 points, 7.2 rebounds and four assists. The scoring punch has been particularly surprising and important for the surging 8-3 Warriors. Lendeborg is making better than 44% of his 5.5 attempted 3s per game and has gained enough trust from Steve Kerr that the coach is putting the basketball in the rookie's hands to make decisions down the stretch of close games. -- Anthony Slater 10. New York Knicks 2026-27 record: 6-4 Previous ranking: 17 Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 11), @ IND (Nov. 13), @ TOR (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: C Andre Drummond At times it has appeared like Drummond has been out of place, with Mike Brown pulling Drummond abruptly in the middle of games for not getting back on defense and trying his hand with James Wiseman instead. But one thing that cannot be denied is Drummond's effect on the glass. The Knicks were supposed to suffer a drop-off as one of the best offensive rebounding teams after Mitchell Robinson departed to Boston. But per 36 minutes, Drummond has averaged over eight offensive rebounds to help the Knicks remain a top-three team in that category. And Brown has complemented Drummond's screen-roll defense recently, noting his physicality. -- Goodwill 11. Portland Trail Blazers 2026-27 record: 7-3 Previous ranking: 8 Next games: vs. OKC (Nov. 11), @ SAC (Nov. 13), @ MIN (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: G Damian Lillard Portland's best newcomer is actually an old friend in Lillard, who is doing his best to make Rip City forget that he was traded to the Bucks in 2023 and missed last season with an Achilles injury. Lillard, 36, is averaging 19.4 points and 4.4 assists, and he has made fast friends with All-Star wing Deni Avdija . The Blazers boast an excellent plus-9.4 net rating when Avdija and Lillard, their two leading scorers, share the court. -- Golliver 12. Denver Nuggets 2026-27 record: 5-4 Previous ranking: 15 Next games: @ MEM (Nov. 11), @ NO (Nov. 14), vs. PHX (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: F Trevon Brazile The Nuggets remain in a perpetual search for lineup combinations that can survive in the minutes either Nikola Jokic or the scorching Jamal Murray are off the floor. Through nine games, they're minus-15 in Jokic's bench time and minus-29 in Murray's. But within that, in their latest search for depth pieces after Peyton Watson 's departure this past summer, they've received encouraging contributions from Brazile and Bryce Hopkins -- both second-rounders from the 2026 draft. Brazile is a 6-10 wing with a 7-4 wingspan, flashing early as a rebounder and a defensive disruptor in a few of Denver's wins. He's averaging 20.3 minutes, a number that might rise as the season progresses. -- Slater 13. Memphis Grizzlies 2026-27 record: 7-3 Previous ranking: 6 Next games: vs. DEN (Nov. 11), @ NO (Nov. 13), vs. @BKN (Nov. 14) Top newcomer: F Cameron Boozer Rookie Cameron Boozer, the third pick of the 2026 draft, is already surprising some opponents with his unexpected agility and scoring prowess. "I had no clue he could move the way he moves, also that he could shoot the way he shoots," said Golden State center Draymond Green on "The Draymond Green Show" podcast. With Isaiah Stewart out due to a right knee bone bruise, Boozer is also having to showcase his versatility by sliding over from his natural power forward spot to center. "We are featuring him in a lot of different sets," Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo said. -- Wright 14. Atlanta Hawks 2026-27 record: 7-5 Previous ranking: 18 Next games: @ CHI (Nov. 13), @ MIL (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Kingston Flemings With the Hawks' offense struggling early in the season, coach Quin Snyder inserted the rookie Flemings into the starting lineup and moved veteran CJ McCollum to a reserve role. The Hawks went on to win three out of the four games with Flemings as starter while ranking fifth in offense. Something to pay attention to is whether Snyder trusts Flemings to close games. In the past four games, he ranks eighth in minutes per game in the fourth quarter. -- Bobby Marks 15. Dallas Mavericks 2026-27 record: 7-4 Previous ranking: 13 Next games: @ MIN (Nov. 12), @ CLE (Nov. 14), @ BOS (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Zaccharie Risacher The Mavericks took a flier on Risacher when they acquired him in the three-way trade that sent Luguentz Dort to Atlanta, hoping they could develop the former No. 1 pick into a quality role player. The 6-9 Risacher has impressed with his defensive activity as a reserve, averaging 1.3 steals and 1.1 blocks per game. Coach Dusty May is comfortable giving Risacher the assignment of guarding elite scorers across multiple positions. His defense on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Kevin Durant helped the Mavs pull off wins over the Thunder and Rockets. -- MacMahon 16. Cleveland Cavaliers 2026-27 record: 5-6 Previous ranking: 9 Next games: @ NYK (Nov. 11), @ MIA (Nov. 13), vs. DAL (Nov. 14) Top newcomer: G Meleek Thomas Headline acquisition Peyton Watson is still struggling to find his footing in Cleveland, but Thomas, picked 34th in the 2026 draft, has been a pleasant surprise for the Cavaliers. The rookie guard shone at summer league and has carried over that performance to games that count, averaging 13 points and hitting 48% of his 3s so far. After starting the season with three DNPs in Cleveland's first five games, Thomas has quickly worked his way into playing 20-plus minutes every night. -- Zach Kram 17. Toronto Raptors 2026-27 record: 5-5 Previous ranking: 14 Next games: vs. BOS (Nov. 11), @ PHI (Nov. 12), vs. NYK (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: F Allen Graves This should be going to Kawhi Leonard , who returned to Toronto in an offseason trade, but he has played only two games this season while sidelined with soreness in his left knee. The reality for the Raptors is that no newcomer has made a significant impact this season, but Graves, the team's first-round pick, has been the best of the team's additions, which include veteran Kyle Anderson and rookie Jaden Bradley . He has reached double digits once this season, scoring 11 points in a loss to Minnesota, and has largely played a depth role. -- Rhim 18. Miami Heat 2026-27 record: 5-6 Previous ranking: 19 Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 13), vs. DET (Nov. 14), vs. HOU (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: F Giannis Antetokounmpo Even with the Heat's early-season struggles, it would be almost malpractice if we left Antetokounmpo off the list. After playing a career-low 36 games last season with Milwaukee, Antetokounmpo has appeared in all 10 games this season. The former MVP has scored 25 points or more in seven games and is on pace to average the most rebounds in his career since 2019-20. He is currently averaging a career-high 3.7 offensive rebounds. -- Marks 19. Washington Wizards 2026-27 record: 4-7 Previous ranking: 16 Next games: @ IND (Nov. 11), vs. DET (Nov. 12), vs. HOU (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: C Anthony Davis The 10-time All-Star counts as a newcomer, right? He technically joined the Wizards last February but didn't play a game for them until this season. All he has done with his new team is average 25.7 points and 9.7 rebounds this season. Washington is 4-5 when Davis plays and 0-2 when he doesn't, including a 39-point shellacking in Oklahoma City without the star big man on the court. -- Kram 20. New Orleans Pelicans 2026-27 record: 4-7 Previous ranking: 22 Next games: vs. BKN (Nov. 11), vs. MEM (Nov. 13), vs. DEN (Nov. 14) Top newcomer: F Trendon Watford Coach Jamahl Mosley has largely relied on familiar faces while juggling his rotation due to injuries. Believe it or not, New Orleans' top eight scorers are all returning members of last year's 26-win team. Watford, a journeyman forward who joined the Pelicans on a minimum contract this summer, has worked his way into Mosley's rotation by averaging 7.2 points and 3.5 rebounds off the bench over the past six games. Meanwhile, Bennedict Mathurin , a 2022 lottery pick who inked a two-year, $15.4 million deal with New Orleans in free agency, is averaging a career-low 15.0 minutes per game. -- Golliver 21. Phoenix Suns 2026-27 record: 4-6 Previous ranking: 24 Next games: vs. CHA (Nov. 12), vs. LAL (Nov. 15), @ DEN (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: C Miles Bridges This year's Suns team, which ranks last in the league in rebounds per game, would be in even worse shape on the boards if not for Bridges securing a career-best 7.8 caroms per game -- two more than he averaged for the Charlotte Hornets last season. The 6-7 forward is also putting up 15.8 points, 3.2 assists and a career-high 1.2 steals per game. After starting the season 1-5, Phoenix won two out of its past three games, with Bridges averaging 9.3 rebounds during that stretch. -- McMenamin 22. Indiana Pacers 2026-27 record: 3-8 Previous ranking: 23 Next games: vs. WAS (Nov. 11), vs. NYK (Nov. 13), @ PHI (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: C Ivica Zubac Injuries have interrupted Zubac's total impact in his new home, but he played one of his best games of the season against the Mavericks this week, despite a modest box score -- 16 points on 5-of-7 shooting, but the team was a plus-6 while he was in the game. In spurts, he has shown there is room for more, especially as the Pacers get accustomed to his game while they await Tyrese Haliburton 's return to the lineup. -- Jamal Collier 23. Charlotte Hornets 2026-27 record: 4-7 Previous ranking: 20 Next games: @ PHX (Nov. 12), @ LAC (Nov. 15), @ LAL (Nov. 17) Top newcomer: G Grayson Allen Allen is averaging 15.3 points for the Hornets while making 47% of his 3-point tries. Charlotte ranks 28th in 3-point percentage as a team, but that's not Allen's fault. He ranks second in individual 3-point percentage (sandwiched between Jamal Murray and Stephen Curry ) out of 77 players with at least 50 attempts. -- Kram 24. Orlando Magic 2026-27 record: 3-7 Previous ranking: 21 Next games: @ UTAH (Nov. 11), vs. MIL (Nov. 13), @ BOS (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: G Tristan Da Silva Da Silva is not considered a newcomer since he was drafted in the 2024 first round. But with the injury to Paolo Banchero , Da Silva is averaging career highs in minutes (30.5) and points (15.1). He is also shooting 40% from 3. Da Silva was a new face to the Magic's starting five on Saturday night as he made his first start of the season in a loss to Golden State. -- Marks 25. LA Clippers 2026-27 record: 2-8 Previous ranking: 25 Next games: vs. OKC (Nov. 13), vs. CHA (Nov. 15), vs. UTAH (Nov. 17) Top newcomer: G Keaton Wagler The 6-5 guard, selected with the No. 5 pick out of Illinois, ranks fifth in 3-point percentage (39.0%) among rookies with at least 30 attempts. He has also found a way to generate points at the line, ranking second in total free throw attempts and second in free throw percentage (86.5%) among rookies with at least 30 trips to the line. As the Clippers begin their rebuild after the lackluster Kawhi Leonard - Paul George era, Wagler's development should be priority No. 1 for the franchise this season. -- McMenamin 26. Brooklyn Nets 2026-27 record: 2-8 Previous ranking: 29 Next games: @ NO (Nov. 11), @ MEM (Nov. 14), vs. PHI (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: F Julius Randle It has been hit or miss for Randle so far this season -- he has had bouts of being the most consistent Net on a team full of developing guards. He has had to create his own offense, which he might prefer, as Mikel Brown Jr . and Egor Demin are also battling injuries. He and Michael Porter Jr . can only play together so much because their styles clash, and on some nights like Sunday against Dallas, he'll be a minus-33 in a 130-93 loss. He's a proud veteran in a tough situation -- not an ideal one -- and the Nets have to find ways to maximize him on this ill-fitting team. -- Goodwill 27. Utah Jazz 2026-27 record: 1-10 Previous ranking: 26 Next games: vs. ORL (Nov. 11), @ HOU (Nov. 13), vs. SAS (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Darryn Peterson After a slow start, Darryn Peterson has started to get cooking, displaying the scoring ability that enticed the Jazz to draft him with the No. 2 pick. He has had his first three 20-point performances in the Jazz's past three games. Peterson has averaged 24 points on 51.9% shooting from the floor (11-of-24 on 3s) over those three games. -- MacMahon 28. Chicago Bulls 2026-27 record: 1-8 Previous ranking: 27 Next games: @ SAS (Nov. 11), vs. ATL (Nov. 13), @ MIN (Nov. 14) Top newcomer: F Caleb Wilson There haven't been many bright spots for the Bulls so far, but Wilson looks like he belongs. The early returns are strong at 19 points and six rebounds per game, yet his potential is tantalizing. He attacks the basket with intent to dunk everything, and his highlights on defense are eye-popping. Wilson isn't used to losing frequently, so with the Bulls in position to keep racking up L's, Chicago is already trying to manage his body language and effort. Tiago Splitter benched him last week against the Knicks because he noticed him getting down after missing some shots. Still, despite the growing pains, Wilson is easily the team's best newcomer. -- Collier 29. Milwaukee Bucks 2026-27 record: 1-10 Previous ranking: 28 Next games: vs. LAL (Nov. 11), @ ORL (Nov. 13), vs. ATL (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Brayden Burries Burries has already replaced Ryan Rollins in the Bucks' starting lineup, and he has easily been the biggest bright spot during a miserable start to the year in Milwaukee. He had the best game of his young career against the Raptors last week with 21 points, 11 rebounds and six assists. He has come out the gates as a great rebounder, and since moving to the starting lineup, he's averaging 13.0 points, 8.0 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 29 minutes. As the Bucks' season continues to slip away, Burries should get even more opportunities. -- Collier 30. Sacramento Kings 2026-27 record: 1-10 Previous ranking: 30 Next games: vs. POR (Nov. 13), vs. OKC (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Darius Acuff Jr. The No. 7 pick has opened his career with 20 or more shot attempts in 10 consecutive games, the longest streak for a rookie since Wilt Chamberlain (19 games) back in 1959. It hasn't all been cloaked in inefficiency, either. Acuff has made 45% or more of those shots in five of the past six games, showing greater comfort and passing willingness. He has games of 10, 12 and 14 assists during that stretch. Acuff recently: "Early on, I wasn't making as many reads. I was forcing a lot of shots. I think the game has slowed down for me." -- Slater

teamStories.summary: With the NBA trade deadline looming, which title contenders should -- and could -- make a deal to improve?
teamStories.detailText: With the start of the 2026-27 NBA regular season in the rearview, the Feb. 11 trade deadline is just over the horizon, and it's never too early to start discussing which teams need to keep their options open and potentially add talent over the next three months. Injuries have plagued the league early on, with the Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves both losing major cornerstones of their roster for an extended period of time. Do these Western Conference contenders need to start filling out their rotations, or can they survive without their superstars until the postseason? And after a shaky start to the season, do the defending champions New York Knicks need to rethink their run back to the Finals with some roster moves? As teams settle into the season, our NBA insiders break down what 10 playoff contenders lack, the constraints shaping their trade options and what's in store as the deadline approaches. Order is based on the top 10 teams in ESPN's Basketball Power Index (BPI) as of Tuesday, Nov. 10. Jump to a contender: BOS | CLE | DET HOU | LAL | MIN NYK | OKC | PHI | SA 1. San Antonio Spurs (10-2) Projected record: 62-20 Chances to make the conference finals: 58.5% What they're missing: The Spurs are on a winning streak even without any games from Tobias Harris , their big offseason acquisition . It's hard to find a hole in one of the league's most complete, well-rounded rosters. Their depth, however, could use some improvement, so they won't be stuck playing deep from their bench with the likes of Jordan McLaughlin if one of their three guards goes down with an injury, as they did in the playoffs last year. -- Zach Kram What they can pull off: The Spurs have the draft assets to swing a deal, but that does not mean general manager Brian Wright will look to be aggressive. With one of the best records last year, San Antonio elected to stand pat. If the Spurs do look to make a move, they have an unprotected 2027 first-round pick from Atlanta and three additional tradeable first-rounders. They also have swap rights in 2028 (via Boston, if Nos. 2-30), 2030 (the most favorable of San Antonio, Dallas, Minnesota (if Nos. 2-30) and 2031 (via Sacramento). San Antonio has 12 tradeable second-rounders. Keep an eye on whether San Antonio is willing to take back salary that stretches past 2026-27. With Victor Wembanyama 's extension starting next season and sixth man Keldon Johnson a free agent, San Antonio is only $11 million below the luxury tax in 2027-28. -- Bobby Marks What's next for San Antonio? San Antonio plans to play out the season with what's on the roster despite owning plenty of assets to make a move at the trade deadline. The Spurs appear to be somewhat thin at the center spot behind Luke Kornet , but the staff has been pleased with the progress made by rookie Tarris Reed Jr . in such a short time. San Antonio understands that over the next two years, the roster could become expensive, with the club expected to sign Stephon Castle to an extension this summer, followed by an extension for Dylan Harper in the summer of 2028. Besides that, the Spurs are already experiencing somewhat of a numbers problem due to all the depth they've accumulated. "There's not enough minutes to go around," coach Mitch Johnson said. "Unfortunately, I've got to play the bad guy and I'm not always going to be right. But I've got to make tough decisions in regards to only 240 minutes." -- Michael C. Wright 2. Oklahoma City Thunder (8-4) Projected record: 58-24 Chances to make the conference finals: 43.5% What they're missing: The Thunder are missing lots of rotation players , and their activity at this trade deadline will depend a great deal on when -- or whether -- they can project those injured players to return. Nique Clifford is another body on the perimeter , but he doesn't seem like a playoff difference-maker, so general manager Sam Presti might still be on the search for another defensively minded wing who can backfill some of the production of the injured Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace . -- Kram What they can pull off: The Nov. 8 trade for Clifford does not eliminate Oklahoma City from making another trade. While the Thunder do not have a roster spot, they do have the $5.4 million expiring contract of Nikola Topic and the $4.9 million salary of a former first-round pick, Thomas Sorber . Because they are over the first apron, Oklahoma City cannot take back additional salary if either player is traded. The Thunder also have three trade exceptions ($5.8, $11.3, $17.7 million), seven tradeable first-round picks (including three in June) and 19 second-rounders. -- Marks What's next for Oklahoma? Presti will be patient. The Thunder addressed the need for defensive-minded wing depth by making a buy-low trade for 2025 first-round pick Clifford, parting with a pair of second-round picks to acquire a player who has two seasons remaining on his rookie deal. Oklahoma City will explore the market for opportunities to upgrade over the next few months, but a big splash would be a big surprise. It's not Presti's style, as the Thunder haven't made a major midseason trade since getting Kendrick Perkins in 2011. Yes, Presti has plenty of picks that could be used to put together a blockbuster deal. But he also has to prioritize future finances with the goal of keeping a contender-quality supporting cast around Shai Gilgeous-Alexander throughout his prime. -- Tim MacMahon 3. Boston Celtics (10-2) Projected record: 59-23 Chances to make the conference finals: 57% What they're missing: The Celtics rank only 22nd in defensive rebounding rate, which is an anomaly for a team coached by Joe Mazzulla. Boston has ranked 11th or better in this stat in every other year with Mazzulla at the helm, per Cleaning the Glass . This issue should be fixable based on Boston's roster, with the likes of Mitchell Robinson and Jayson Tatum -- an excellent rebounder for his position -- chipping in. If it continues, Boston might be in the market for another big body who can help grab rebounds in the playoffs. -- Kram What they can pull off: Last season, the Celtics were one of the league's more active teams ahead of the trade deadline. The four separate trades dropped Boston below the luxury tax while also creating a $27.7 million trade exception. The exception is available until February, but the first apron hard cap prevents Boston from using more than $10 million of it. This year, the Celtics do not have to trim payroll but do need to keep an eye on the luxury tax, which they are currently $1.75 million below. Boston's most valuable asset could be its open roste spot. Because they are below the first apron, the Celtics will be able to sign a waived player with a preexisting salary of $15 million or more -- Marks What's next for Boston? Finding another big man could be high on the Celtics' list. One thing the Celtics have learned from the Knicks is not overtaxing Mitchell Robinson , who plays well in spurts, and keeping him around the 20-minute mark is ideal. Keeping Tatum and Paul George fresh would be paramount as well, especially with Tatum still working his way back to his new normal in his first full season following an Achilles injury in 2025. The $27 million trade exception could go a long way, especially if they view the Eastern Conference as winnable. -- Vincent Goodwill 4. Houston Rockets (9-3) Projected record: 55-27 Chances to make the conference finals: 23.8% What they're missing: Only two Rockets perimeter players are shooting better than 37% on 3-pointers this season, and one of them is Bogdan Bogdanovic , whose injury track record suggests it might not be safe to count on him over the full season. Kevin Durant and Reed Sheppard should improve as the season continues, but it might behoove Houston to grab one more shooter in the meantime. -- Kram What they can pull off: The Rockets have two appealing trade assets in this upcoming draft: the right to swap with Brooklyn and an unprotected first-round pick (via the Phoenix Suns ). Houston has four additional first-round picks available to trade, a $13.3 million trade exception and an open roster spot. The Rockets are allowed to use the full exception and still exceed the first apron. -- Marks What's next for Houston? Despite owning plenty of assets and a trade exception, it's likely Houston will continue -- like last season -- to refrain from making any moves. Especially now that its roster has been revamped with the offseason additions of Bogdanovic and Marcus Smart , along with the return of point guard Fred VanVleet . The overall size throughout the roster gives the Rockets plenty of flexibility to utilize multiple lineups and combinations of players without sacrificing production and performance. VanVleet's absence last season somewhat sped up the development of Sheppard, Amen Thompson , Tari Eason and Jabari Smith Jr . Still, Houston could probably use some depth at the center position, given the injury concerns regarding Steven Adams (right calf strain) and Clint Capela (right ankle sprain), who are both expected to return to the lineup soon. But unless the Rockets encounter a deal they can't refuse at the deadline, it's likely they stand pat. -- Wright 5. New York Knicks (6-5) Projected record: 54-28 Chances to make the conference finals: 42% What they're missing: The Knicks had, by definition, a championship-level roster last season, and the only player they lost was Robinson. Andre Drummond has served as a serviceable replacement so far , and it's difficult to imagine New York finding many better options on the trade market. But if one presents itself, then that's the clearest spot on New York's roster worth improving. -- Kram What they can pull off: The Knicks faced the same limitations last season but were still able to trade for backup guard Jose Alvarado . This season, New York is $809,000 below the second apron and is not allowed to sign a player until Feb. 14. The Knicks can use Pacome Dadiet 's $3 million expiring contract in a trade but cannot take back more salary. New York is not allowed to sign a player waived who had a preexisting salary of $15 million or more. The Knicks have one first-round pick and 12 second-rounders available to trade. -- Marks What's next for New York? The Knicks are putting off contract issues until the offseason and there's not a lot of flexibility, especially with owner James Dolan proclaiming he won't go into the second apron . If Mikal Bridges continues to struggle, do the Knicks start to canvas the league? But then again, he's owed over $116.5 million over the next three seasons, including a player option in 2029-30. The hope is that he turns it around similar to last season, because this team is in need of shot creation and shotmaking. -- Goodwill 6. Los Angeles Lakers (11-2) Projected record: 54-28 Chances to make the conference finals: 13.9% What they're missing: The Lakers have the best offense in the league but rank in the bottom half on the other end of the floor, and specifically they're 28th in defensive rebounding rate, ahead of only the Bulls and Suns. Kevon Looney is not the answer at backup center behind Walker Kessler , and although Sandro Mamukelashvili is a decent option, it's safe to add the Lakers to the long list of teams that could use another competent bruiser on their bench. -- Kram What they can pull off: The Lakers depleted their draft assets in the Kessler sign-and-trade which left them with the right to swap their 2028 first-rounder as their most significant remaining draft asset. The Lakers have three tradeable second-rounders (from 2031 to 2033, with two belonging to the Washington Wizards). From a roster standpoint, Los Angeles could look to package the contracts of Jaden Hardy ($6 million) and Jarred Vanderbilt ($12.4 million) for a player earning $26 million or below. Despite being hard-capped at the first apron, the Lakers are $8.1 million under and are allowed to take back additional salary. Los Angeles has 15 guaranteed contracts and would need to waive or trade a player to open a roster spot. -- Marks What's next for Los Angeles? After looking into trade packages to clear up a roster spot during the preseason, the Lakers ultimately had to waive former first-round pick Dalton Knecht in order to cut down to the maximum 15-player allotment. Coach JJ Redick has pretty much stuck to a 10-man rotation so far, with Vanderbilt overtaking Looney in the depth chart when Mamukelashvili isn't in as the stretch 5. Redick still has to see what he has in second-year forward Adou Thiero and rookie Cameron Carr , although neither figures to be the solution to L.A. ranking second-to-last in the league in rebounding. Still, as one Eastern Conference executive told ESPN, "so long as Doncic, [Austin] Reaves and Kessler stay healthy, the Lakers will be fine." Reaves is now dealing with a left heel injury that forced him to exit the team's win over the Bucks on Wednesday night. -- Dave McMenamin 7. Minnesota Timberwolves (8-3) Projected record: 54-28 Chances to make the conference finals: 26% What they're missing: Entering the season, it seemed as if the Timberwolves' big issue was going to be frontcourt depth after they traded Julius Randle and Naz Reid in the offseason. But second-year Frenchman Joan Beringer has done an excellent job backing up his countryman, Rudy Gobert , and Trey Lyles , after a season out of the NBA, has performed surprisingly well at the backup power forward spot. Does Minnesota trust that that will continue, though, or would the team rather pursue a sure thing at the position? -- Kram What they can pull off: The Timberwolves were one of the big winners last February when they acquired Ayo Dosunmu . Because of that trade and the offseason addition of LaMelo Ball , Minnesota's draft assets are limited. They have no first-round picks available to trade and one second-rounder (2030 via Memphis; if Nos. 51-60). One player to watch could be Cody Williams , who is on an expiring $6 million contract after Minnesota declined his team option for next season. Apron rules prevent Minnesota from taking back more salary than they send out, so the return of Donte DiVincenzo , who tore his Achilles during the 2026 playoffs, could be the Timberwolves' big addition at the deadline. -- Marks What's next for Minnesota? Keep biding time until Anthony Edwards ' return. Minnesota should be thrilled with how it has played since its franchise guard underwent knee surgery after playing just four games to start the season. The Timberwolves are 5-2 without Edwards and boast the NBA's top-ranked defense. The schedule will get tougher, but they have held up well in the face of a potentially season-altering injury. Ball continues to assimilate well to his new surroundings after an offseason trade, and fellow newcomer Jonathan Kuminga has made a good first impression after so-so stops with the Warriors and Hawks. Meanwhile, Dosunmu has been excellent as Edwards' stand-in replacement. With Edwards projected to return as soon as late December or early January, Minnesota should have plenty of time to evaluate its full roster before the Feb. 11 trade deadline. -- Ben Golliver 8. Detroit Pistons (7-3) Projected record: 55-27 Chances to make the conference finals: 44.4% What they're missing: The Pistons' greatest need is the same as it has been for the last 18 months: a second scorer and playmaker next to Cade Cunningham . Duncan Robinson is the only other perimeter player averaging more than 12 points per game. And although Daniss Jenkins has done an admirable job as a backup, he's not a championship-level No. 2 option. Luckily, the Pistons have plenty of trade assets they could use in a deal for a fellow star. -- Kram What they can pull off: The Pistons are among a handful of teams that control each of their next seven first-round picks. They can trade up to four and can swap in each season. Detroit also has 11 seconds available. And, despite $90 million committed to Cunningham and Jalen Duren this season, Detroit is $14.5 million under the first apron hard cap. However, putting together a trade package without including a starter or key rotation piece could be difficult. To match salary, the Pistons have only the sizable contracts of John Collins ($17 million), Robinson ($16 million) and Isaiah Joe ($11.3 million). None have guaranteed salary obligations past this season. For Detroit to use its $5.2 million or $15 million trade exception, it would need to open a roster spot. -- Marks What's next for Detroit? The Pistons once again look poised to be among the top teams in the East during the regular season, even without making a move at the deadline. A year ago at the deadline, with a young team playing better than expected, Detroit chose not to rock the boat. This front office has chosen patience in letting its core of young players grow so far, so it's worth watching if an opportunity presents itself for a bigger swing and how the Pistons handle it this time around. -- Jamal Collier 9. Philadelphia 76ers (9-3) Projected record: 49-33 Chances to make the conference finals: 21.1% What they're missing: The 76ers don't have proper championship-level depth at center behind Joel Embiid , who is the single greatest injury risk for any team in the championship picture. Lineups with LeBron James at center can function on occasion, but that's not a permanent solution, and with Ariel Hukporti out for the season after tearing his Achilles , Philadelphia needs a better backup big man ahead of Jabari Walker and Adem Bona . -- Kram What they can pull off: The 76ers have an open roster spot and Hukporti's $3.4 million expiring contract. Because they are $1.8 million under the first apron hard cap, they are allowed to take back up to $5.2 million of salary. They also have 10 second-round picks available to use in a trade. Philadelphia can sign a player with its open roster spot starting on Dec. 4. -- Marks What's next for Philadelphia? Coach Nick Nurse said that big man Dominick Barlow , who has missed all of this season with a back injury, is expected to be cleared for on-court activities by mid-November. The Sixers are thin in the frontcourt, with Bona missing time with a neck injury, Hukporti out for the season and Tacko Fall missing time with a quad injury. For now, the Sixers have been excited by how Walker has played as the team's backup center. Walker, too, missed time with a knee injury but has proven to be the team's most consistent backup center option this season. He had his best game this season in a win over the Bulls, finishing with nine points and 11 rebounds. "He probably deserves to play more, to be honest," Nurse said this season. -- Kris Rhim 10. Cleveland Cavaliers (6-6) Projected record: 47-35 Chances to make the conference finals: 11.8% What they're missing: Cleveland ranks 29th in the league in defensive turnover rate, per Cleaning the Glass, ahead of only the woeful Milwaukee defense. This is still a decent defensive unit overall, thanks to the efforts of Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen near the rim. But Cleveland's backcourt looks tremendously exploitable in the playoffs; even reserves Sam Merrill and rookie Meleek Thomas are more offensively minded. The Cavaliers are in desperate need of another perimeter stopper. -- Kram What they can pull off: Five players (Mobley, Allen, Donovan Mitchell , Peyton Watson and James Harden ) combine to earn 85% of the cap this season, making a trade difficult unless they are willing to part ways with Allen, or reserves Merrill and Jaylon Tyson . The Cavaliers are $45,000 below the first apron this season and have no tradeable first-round picks and only one second-rounder available. Cleveland can fill their open roster spot starting on April 9. -- Marks What's next for Cleveland? After Harden took the place of Darius Garland at last season's deadline, the Cavs brought back their core four, believing that continuity will make a difference this season. But Cleveland is currently leaning on some younger players, such as Tyson, Thomas and Tyrese Proctor to fill out its depth off the bench. Keep an eye out for whether that trio can continue to produce or if the Cavs will look for moves similar to last season's deadline when they added veterans such as Dennis Schroder and Keon Ellis in an attempt to fortify their depth. -- Collier

teamStories.summary: The Law of Averages may be a myth, but there is logic behind it, and it showed last night.
teamStories.detailText: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 11: Dylan Harper #2 of the San Antonio Spurs and Caleb Wilson #8 of the Chicago Bulls battle for a rebound during the first half at United Center on November 11, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s this popular belief known as the Law of Averages. While it’s not a recognized theorem in the mathematical world, it’s a common saying that refers to the idea that if something happens more or less often than it should, logic says things will eventually balance back out and return to normal. It’s a fallacy in the gambling world; if you keep flipping a coin and it keeps landing on tails, that doesn’t mean the odds are better it will land on heads the next time because each individual flip is a separate event with no relationship to another. The same applies if you keep starting a card game over with a full or new deck — your odds of winning don’t improve just because it’s been a while since you last won, because this hand has no relationship to the last. However, one place where averages and the “laws” that go with them do often apply is basketball. While still technically a mathematical fallacy, one thing about sports is more than anything, it comes down to talent, and across a large sample size, the numbers do in fact tell a story. Sure, each individual game is a separate event from each other, but it’s the same players with the same skillset going through the same motions, so there is in fact a relationship across the separate events, and more often than not, they will do close to what the numbers say they will. Of course, there are always outliers and unexpected events — sports wouldn’t be any fun if everything always went as expected — and that’s exactly what happened last night in the first half between the San Antonio Spurs and Chicago Bulls. The Spurs were on a nine-game winning against what we can all probably admit is not the most difficult stretch of schedule ever, but they were walking into a potential trap game considering it was against a team on a seven-game losing streak, and the Law of Averages says one of those streaks is getting closer to ending, right? It was also the end of a four-game road trip, things have been too easy on said-trip, and they may have been looking ahead to Friday’s Cup match against the Warriors (which may have lost some luster if Steph Curry is out after appearing to injure his abdomen last night against the Rockets). Other than a flurry from three and a hot start from De’Aaron Fox briefly keeping them in it, the Spurs quickly found themselves falling behind while the Bulls were insanely hot through the first 18 minutes of the game. They shot 17-20 (or 85%) from the field in the first quarter and at one point were shooting 83% from both the field AND three in the second. While the Spurs’ effort wasn’t what you’d call admirable, I was never too worried during the first half because I knew the Law of Averages would eventually take over. No team, not even the Warriors of a decade ago, can keep up those types of numbers for an entire game, let alone a team as bad as these Bulls. They got the lead as high as 22 in the first half, but the Spurs weathered the storm and waited for their numbers to start averaging back to the mean while knowing they had a another gear they could turn on. They used a run before halftime to cut the deficit to a very manageable 14 points while the Bulls’ numbers starting dropping (they were “only” shooting 67% by the midway mark), took their presumed licking from Mitch Johnson in the locker room, then came out firing in the second half. As the Spurs returned to their normal selves, the Bulls were understandably overwhelmed, knowing they had already given their best shot and the Law of Averages had now taken its hold. Victor Wembanyama went back to demoralizing teams with an unstoppable presence at the rim, balanced out by taking (and making) timely jumpers within the flow of the offense. By the end of the game, everything was as it should be: the Spurs won while shooting 50% from the field (38% from three), and while the Bulls still ended with impressive final numbers (58% and 52%, respectively) thanks to their otherworldly first half, they made five fewer field goals thanks in part to coughing the ball up 19 times compared to the Spurs’ 6. The Law of Averages was alive and well for the Spurs 10th straight victory. Or, you know, maybe that had nothing to do with it at all and there was just something off with the Bulls’ court. You could have watched that game and simply concluded that, based on the massive swings in shooting each team took from half-to-half, “Right rim good, left rim bad.” Takeaways “Oh, Wemby had 32 points on 13-18 shooting, 9 rebounds and 5 blocks? Ho hum, just another day at the office.” Yes, we have reached that point with him. His numbers have been so outlandish and even historical lately that I hardly even noticed him last night. And while it’s fun to see opposing fans oohing and awing, we’re just like, “He dunked from the free throw line? Nothing new.” You know how else you know someone has arrived at greatness? When the haters start hating. “He’s 7’7”, he should have a post game to be great!” Wemby starts dominating in the paint: “So what? He’s just tall!” The funniest “rage” tweet I saw recently was one dude complaining that he can “only” handle 25 minutes per game, so he must not be in good shape. No bro, that’s just a result of all the blowouts and him not needing any more minutes. And if he was playing into extended garbage time, you’d just accuse him of stat padding. As the old saying goes, “Haters gonna hate, Spurs gonna win”. I think it’s officially time that we put Fox’s poor finals performance behind us. We all know he was playing on one leg, and while he had a couple of massive gaffes, he wasn’t the only one who messed up or cost them the series; it was a team effort. (I even pointed out in a comment on a Feed post yesterday that had the Finals gone any further, Wemby would have a Draymond Green mark on his legacy because he more than likely would have been suspended for Game 6 for flagrant accumulation — and that was after he was lucky to avoid it after Game 3. The league wasn’t going to bail him out twice.) But back to Fox, he has been a tremendous steadying present for this still-young squad, with Stephon Castle in a bit of a funk right now and Dylan Harper playing very well overall but still streaky from quarter to quarter. It’s time we get back to remembering and appreciating the good Fox brings, which far outweighs a couple of bad plays on a bum ankle. The strength of schedule of the Spurs’ start to the season may not be the strongest, but it has been exhausting, at least for me. Three back-to-backs in the first 10 games, 12 of the first 20 with tip-off times at 8:00 or later — it’s been brutal for my sleep schedule. That’s why last night’s 7:00 tip-off time was the most amazing feeling ever. I watched, it ended, then I went to bed at my normal time (or what now feels early), and I’m relatively fresh for a Thursday morning. The good news is after game 20 — 8:30 against the Lakers on Black Friday — the Spurs won’t have another game with a tip-off time later than 7 until #42 on January 20: their first game back from the Europe trip.

stories.title: Vikings 'hyped' to welcome back 'leader' Cousins on 1st day of practice
stories.summary: The Minnesota Vikings reveled Thursday in quarterback Kirk Cousins' first full day back with the organization.
stories.detailText: EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings reveled Thursday in quarterback Kirk Cousins ' first full day back with the organization. Their operations staff opened practice by playing Creed's "Higher" on the team's outdoor speakers, drawing knowing smirks from the handful of players and coaches who remember it as Cousins' anthem during the 2023 season. "It got me hyped," right tackle Brian O'Neill said. "It felt like it raised the temperature outside a few degrees." Rookie safety Jakobe Thomas gave up his No. 8 free of charge, saying afterward that "I just want him to come help us win games." And receiver Justin Jefferson described the day as "a joy to hear him just take over and be a leader in the meeting room, on the field." The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders hours before Tuesday's trade deadline, in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick. He spent Wednesday meeting with coach Kevin O'Connell and other members of the staff, but O'Connell did not hold a practice so that players could have an additional recovery day following their 23-6 loss Monday night to the Buffalo Bills . In replacing former starter Kyler Murray , the 6-2 Vikings are hoping to elevate their passing offense and reverse a two-game losing streak. If that is going to happen, it will be through Cousins' connection with Jefferson. During their last full season together in 2022, Jefferson earned the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year award with career highs in catches (128) and yards (1,809). Upon hearing about the trade Tuesday, Jefferson said his immediate reaction was to flash back to the volume of their previous connection. But Jefferson insisted Thursday that he has not let himself envision any specifics for their reunion. Through Week 9, Jefferson ranks No. 53 in the NFL in receptions (31) and No. 34 in yards per game (56.1) while playing with Murray for five starts and Carson Wentz for two. "At this moment, it's really no expectations," Jefferson said. "It's really just going out there and just executing our plays. It's not really getting too juiced up about him being here or anybody being back there. It's just all about understanding the plays that are being called, understanding the jobs that we have and executing our responsibilities. And just the plays that are there, and the plays that could be made, we just need to continue to just make those type of plays. And I'm pretty sure that the results would be a lot better. "He just understands the game. He's a guy that studies the game a lot. He understands how the defenses play, especially covering me. And he understands, the plays that we have called that are kind of my plays and he understands the timing and the windows to throw those type of plays, but he also doesn't force those type of plays to me and he just lets the game come to me." According to Jefferson and others, Cousins didn't waste any time Thursday stepping into his new role. "He's being vocal," Jefferson said, "just making sure that everybody hears the plays that he's talking about and the notes that he has for certain routes, certain plays. And he's just making sure that everybody's on the same page. So it's definitely cool to hear that type of leadership and command. If you know Kirk, that's pretty normal from him. So it's definitely kind of cool him being back in that room and him taking that control." O'Neill found himself slipping back into old routines as well. "Some of the stuff that you see, you're like, 'Oh, yeah, I'm used to it,'" O'Neill said. "Just the way he gets into the huddle, takes a knee. He's talking with his hands. That felt very familiar. And just the general intensity about him in terms of just little things. I mean, he's on full tilt all the time. There's some things that felt comforting knowing different cadences, knowing just the tone in his voice. Those things haven't really changed."

stories.title: Rams put WR Puka Nacua on IR with knee, toe injuries
stories.summary: The Rams, who had said they would not put Puka Nacua on IR, pivoted so they can sign Brennan Presley to the active roster and Tyler Scott to the practice squad.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES -- The Rams put wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve after all Thursday. Nacua injured the MCL in his right knee and a toe in Sunday's victory over the Washington Commanders and is expected to sit out what coach Sean McVay called "an extended period of time." On Wednesday, McVay had said that because of roster mechanics, the Rams would keep Nacua on the active roster. But on Thursday, the Rams pivoted so they can sign receiver Brennan Presley to the active roster and sign receiver Tyler Scott to the practice squad. Nacua will sit out at least four games while on injured reserve, at the Arizona Cardinals , at home against the Green Bay Packers and Kansas City Chiefs , and at the San Francisco 49ers . In seven games this season, Nacua has 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns. He sat out Weeks 2 and 3 because of a hip injury. Nacua's 70 receptions are the most through a player's first seven games of a season in NFL history, according to ESPN Research. The Rams (5-4) also are without wide receiver Davante Adams , who has been on injured reserve since rupturing a hamstring muscle late in the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.

stories.title: Rams change course, place wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve
stories.summary: After initially saying they wouldn't put wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve, the Rams changed course.
stories.detailText: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is swarmed by Chargers defenders for a short gain during a Rams win on Nov. 1 at SoFi Stadium. (Robert Gauthier / Los Angeles Times) The Rams on Thursday placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve, meaning the star receiver must sit out at least four games. Nacua was injured last Sunday on the Rams’ final play of their 20-13 victory over the Washington Commanders . Nacua, who had 14 receptions for 150 yards and a touchdown, was hit while carrying the ball on a jet sweep. The Rams have experienced a flurry of injuries, and NFL rules limit teams from activating more than eight players a year from injured reserve. Read more: NFL Week 10 picks: Packers prevail over Vikings; Steelers beat Bengals On Wednesday, McVay said Nacua would not be placed on injured reserve because of “semantics with the roster and things like that,” but that he “still is going to be out for an extended period of time.” Last week, the Rams activated running back Ronnie Rivers and edge rusher Myles Garrett from injured reserve. The Rams also opened the 21-day window for tight end Terrance Ferguson to return from an ankle injury, and then Ferguson suffered a hamstring injury. Defensive lineman Kobie Turner could return before the Rams play the Green Bay Packers the night before Thanksgiving, and receiver Davante Adams might return after the Rams play the Packers, McVay has said. Read more: With NFL's toughest schedule looming, Rams quiet at trade deadline as rivals make deals Nacua will be sidelined for Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals, and games against the Packers, Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers. He will not be eligible to return until the Rams Dec. 20 game against the Dallas Cowboys at SoFi Stadium. The Rams elevated receiver Brennan Presley to the roster from the practice squad and signed receiver Tyler Scott to the practice squad. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith and rookie CJ Daniels are other receivers in the roster. stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams have placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve, the team announced Thursday. The move will sideline the receiver for at least four games after he suffered multiple injuries last week. In a connected move, the Rams have signed receiver Brennan Presley to the active roster from the practice squad, and signed WR Tyler Scott to the practice squad. He was later diagnosed with MCL and PCL sprains on his right knee as well as a turf toe injury. Head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Wednesday that Nacua will miss "a significant period of time" with the injuries. McVay initially said that the receiver would not go on IR due to "some semantics with the roster," but that appears to have changed. By being on IR, the earliest that Nacua could return is against the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 20. Nacua, who missed two games early in the season with a hip injury, has had a strong 2026 season up to this point. In seven games, he's caught 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns. The Commanders' game was his most productive of the season before the injuries, as the receiver picked up 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown. Nacua joins fellow Rams receiver Davante Adams, on IR; Adams has been there since Week 6 with a ruptured hamstring. stories.detailText: A day after Sean McVay said the Rams wouldn’t place Puka Nacua on injured reserve, the wide receiver went on IR. McVay said “roster semantics” would keep Nacua on the 53-man roster, with every team getting only eight designated-to-return slots during the season. The Rams have used three of their designations and have Kobie Turner, Davante Adams, Terrance Ferguson and now Nacua on IR with hopes of returning. But with Nacua set to miss "extended time," as McVay said Wednesday, with MCL and PCL sprains in his knee and turf toe, the Rams opted to move him to the IR list. Nacua will miss at least the next four games, with the Cowboys game on Dec. 20 the earliest he can return by rule. The Rams signed wide receiver Brennan Presley to take Nacua's roster spot and added wide receiver Tyler Scott to the practice squad.

stories.detailText: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Cleveland Browns defense has been feeling the pressure through the first nine weeks of the season. Following the complete team meltdown in Week 1 against Jacksonville, the defense has carried more than its share of the water each week. It has become a familiar script: the defense keeps the Browns in the game while the offense bumbles its way through the first three quarters, only to catch fire when it appears all hope is lost to pull out a win. At least that is how it has played out with Deshaun Watson as the starting quarterback. Unfortunately for the Browns, Watson was sidelined for last week’s game against the New Orleans Saints with a concussion, so no winning comeback was to be found. While everyone knows that playing the way the Browns have through the first nine games is not sustainable, most weeks it felt that way given the way the defense was playing. But the strain has started to show on the defense over the past few weeks; in the previous three games, they have allowed an average of 24.7 points and 167 rushing yards per game. So what can the defense do to get itself right and help the Browns avoid heading into the bye week on a three-game losing streak? staying disciplined pic.twitter.com/Qd3eov0HhA — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 12, 2026 When asked about it on Thursday, defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg said it comes down to facing the challenge head-on and finding that extra bit of energy to make a difference : “No one drive defines a game, and I think that’s important for the whole team to know, and that’s what Monk always talks about. Whether it’s starting fast, finishing faster, making the play at the end of the half, going in, getting a three and out after halftime. Each little six-second play defines the game. “And then of course at the end of the game, great defenses try their butts off to finish. And during the week, I’m not going to get into what we do, but what I can promise you is we are always addressing whatever came up head-on, honestly, together, and figuring out the best ways, whether it’s in a meeting, whether it’s out at practice, whether it’s a drill. We do all that, and our guys are bought into that, and it’s really cool to see.” But what about the run defense? While the Browns have never really been stout against the run, being ranked No. 27 against it (130.6 yards per game) this season doesn’t make life any easier. we are the engine pic.twitter.com/4mDb0ZASSM — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 12, 2026 The Texas don’t present a daunting challenge as they are ranked No. 29 in rushing (87.1 yards per game), but neither did the Saints, and they ripped off 141 rushing yards. Rutenberg went back to his standby answer when asked about what the coaches can do this week to get things back on track : “Every week, whatever it is, we address it, like I always say, because that’s just what football is. And in terms of the run defense, great run games are based on violence, which is what we’re built off of. Discipline fits and straining of the ball. And we’ll continue to preach our style of strain and violence and our style of the mind to do our best in the fits, practice it like we’ve been doing it, and continue to, whatever it is, take that approach in everything we’re trying to fix.” The joy of being 5-2 and first in the AFC North has started to slip away over the past two weeks, and the defense has played a role in that. This week presents another challenge, and if the Browns hope to enter the bye with a victory, they are going to need the defense to get back to its particular strain of violence when the Texans have the ball. stories.title: GM Joe Hortiz says Chargers were listening to trade offers, none were enticing
stories.summary: GM Joe Hortiz pushed back against any narrative that the Chargers were unwilling or reluctant to pick up their phone ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.
stories.detailText: EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz said Thursday that he did not field any "particularly serious" trade calls for players on his roster, outside of the since-rescinded deal with the Denver Broncos for linebacker Daiyan Henley . He also said he still feels like the 0-8 Chargers will make it into the win column this season. "I feel like we can win this year," Hortiz said. "I really do. It just hasn't gone our way ... we got to get the breaks to go our way." The Chargers (0-8) will forge ahead against the Ravens (4-5) on "Monday Night Football" with the same roster they had ahead of the trade deadline, including Henley, who is expected to face Baltimore. Hortiz pushed back against any narrative that the Chargers were unwilling or reluctant to pick up their phone ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. "I've been on the phone since Week 3 talking to teams," Hortiz said. "They've inquired about players' availabilities. I've said, 'Hey, this player, no, we're not trading.' Would we consider something? Yes, but it would have to be a good package for us to move them. No one put together any packages that blew us away or that inspired us to continue." Hortiz said he did not receive many calls on individual players, but that there was interest in some players he considers core to the Chargers' future and would not consider moving. "There were some players that you're just not going to trade," Hortiz said. "I'm not trading Justin [Herbert] , right? No one ever called on Justin, but I'm not trading Justin. I'm not trading Ladd [McConkey] . I'm not trading Joe [Alt] . I'm not trading Derwin [James Jr.] . It's just not happening. Tarheeb Still , these players that have futures with us. And a lot of those guys, people didn't call on them." After making back-to-back playoff appearances under coach Jim Harbaugh, the Chargers are in the midst of an 11-game losing streak, including playoffs, dating to last season. They're the lone NFL team without a win this season. Their offense ranks last in the league, averaging only 15.1 points per game, since Mike McDaniel was hired as coordinator ahead of the season. Herbert's total QBR ranks last among qualified passers. He has thrown for six touchdowns with 11 interceptions. The defense also has fallen short, allowing an average of 27.4 points per game, which ranks 28th. "Our job is to continue to fight this year," Hortiz said. "But also have a team that we feel that we can go out there and be successful in the future, too. And so to sit here and say, 'Oh, we're having a bad year. We should get rid of anybody,' that just doesn't seem like a smart way to build for the future as well. So you got to look at it this year and in the future."

stories.title: Vikings sign former Green Bay Packer
stories.summary: Damon Bankston, who was in the RB room when the Packers last faced Minnesota, is now a Viking
stories.detailText: (Photo by Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings signed running back Damon Bankston, a former Green Bay Packer, to the team’s practice squad this week. Bankston spent Weeks 1- 7 with Green Bay, over two stints, before the team needed space on their own practice squad. This addition is interesting, as Bankston could have some info on how the Packers want to attack the Vikings’ pressures. As we all know, Minnesota blitzes at a crazy rate. According to Pro-Football-Reference , they have the Vikings down with a 67.6 percent blitz rate, with the next highest team in the league being the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at 37.2 percent. Because of the extra blitzers, many offenses allocate extra blockers to face the Vikings, most notably running backs. Bankston was not only in Green Bay when the team prepared to play Minnesota in Week 1, but he could also have information on the adjustments the protections made coming out of that game. If I were defensive coordinator Brian Flores, I’d want to pick the brain of the new addition, wouldn’t you? The Packers made a similar addition to their practice squad ahead of their Week 1 matchup against the Vikings — which could be viewed as gamesmanship. Green Bay signed safety Kahlef Hailassie, who has been with Minnesota since 2025, ahead of the season opener. Hailassie is no longer with the Packers. We’ll have to see how long Bankston sticks with the Vikings, or if they only wanted his services for this particular week.

stories.title: Steelers and Bengals meet for AFC North lead on Sunday night, both 6-2
stories.summary: Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals have been on a record run during their four-game winning streak.
stories.detailText: Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals have been on a record run during their four-game winning streak. The only things that may slow them down heading into Sunday night's AFC North showdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers are the NFL scheduling office and jet lag. The Bengals and Steelers are tied atop the division with a 6-2 record. Cincinnati is off to its best start since 2015 after a 31-17 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid. It is also the first time they have won four straight and scored at least 30 points. Pittsburgh has won four straight and five of its past six. It comes into the game rested after having its bye last week. Teams are 5-0 when coming off a bye and their opponent played the week before in an international game. It is 3-0 when that opponent's game was in Europe. This is the second straight year the Steelers are coming off a bye and facing a team that played internationally. Even though the Bengals are fighting history, coach Zac Taylor does think facing a division opponent offers some benefits. “You're able to get started a little quicker because you know the personnel. You’re always going to make sure you comb through the scheme of what they’re doing, and they’ve evolved as the season goes,” Taylor said. Burrow leads the league in completion rate, passing yards per game and passing touchdowns. He passed for 282 yards and three touchdowns during the first meeting on Sept. 27, but Derrick Harmon’s strip-sack on Cincinnati’s final drive allowed Pittsburgh to hold on for a 30-27 victory. The seventh-year franchise quarterback has at least three TD passes in each of the past four games. Tee Higgins has hauled in five touchdowns during the Bengals' winning streak, and Ja’Marr Chase has 32 receptions for 435 yards and four touchdowns. “Some guys would rather play at 1. I’d rather play every game, Sunday night, ‘Monday Night Football.’ I want to be able to showcase what we do and how hard we work. This is a big moment for it,” Burrow said. The Bengals' defense has struggled against the run and when going up against Jaylen Warren . The Steelers' fifth-year running back has two 100-yard games in the past three meetings against the Bengals, who are 25th in the league in run defense and allowing an NFL-high 5.04 yards per carry. Warren is in the midst of a career year and leads the NFL with 5.92 yards per carry. He had 176 yards from scrimmage in the first meeting with Cincinnati. Pittsburgh's passing game has struggled to generate much downfield, but Aaron Rodgers could get one of his top options back this week in wide receiver Michael Pittman, who has been sidelined the past four weeks because of a foot injury. Rodgers has been pleased with Pittsburgh's start, but realizes the focus remains on what they can accomplish down the road. “When you win, sometimes you can gloss over some areas that need improvement if you want to get to where you want to get to, so I think that’s the important thing that experience gives you, is that even though we are 6-2, we’re playing for the division lead again this week," he said. "We need to hold ourselves to a standard of winning in the playoffs and winning in January and February, and we need to climb to that standard.” Tomlin gets to see former team Sunday night's game also marks the first time that Mike Tomlin will see his former team in person. Tomlin led the Steelers for 19 seasons before resigning at the end of last season and joining NBC Sports as an analyst for its pregame, halftime and postgame coverage. “I look forward to it because of the relationship, but you know me, I’m capable of compartmentalizing and getting hyper-focused on the job,” Tomlin said during a teleconference on Wednesday. “It certainly will be fun to see some guys I’ve got relationships with. There will certainly be a lot of those. But they have a job to do, I have a job to do. So, I’m sure everyone is going to be focused on the task at hand.” Need to know Pittsburgh (6-2) at Cincinnati (6-2) When/where to watch: Sunday, 8:20 p.m. EST, NBC. Latest odds: Bengals by 3 1/2 Against the spread: Steelers 6-2; Bengals 4-4 Last week: Steelers had a bye; Bengals beat the Falcons 31-17 in Madrid Last meeting: Steelers beat Bengals 30-27, on Sept. 27, 2026, in Pittsburgh. Series record: Steelers lead 73-41 Matchup to watch Pittsburgh RB Jaylen Warren vs. Cincinnati LBs Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr .: Warren is averaging 64.4 yards after contact in the rushing game and also had 49 receiving yards in the first meeting. Carter and Knight have struggled in coverage as well as being consistent in tackling. Both have nine missed tackles. Stats and stuff — This is the seventh time the Steelers and Bengals have met with first place in the AFC North on the line. In five of the previous six instances, the winner went on to take the division that season. — Pittsburgh's 18 road wins on Sunday night are tied with Green Bay for the second most in the NFL. — Aaron Rodgers' 85 touchdown passes on Sunday night are the most. — Pittsburgh has sacked Burrow 24 times in eight meetings with the 2020 No. 1 overall pick. The Steelers are tied for fourth in the NFL with 26 sacks this season entering Week 10. — Cincinnati is the only team this season that ranks in the top five both in red zone offensive TD percent (22 of 32, 68.8%) and red zone defensive TD percent (12 of 28, 42.9%). — Cincinnati's Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins and Mike Gesicki are the second trio in NFL history to each have at least six receiving touchdowns through a team’s first eight games of a season. The other was Wes Welker, Julius Thomas and Demaryius Thomas of the 2013 Denver Broncos . ------ AP Sports Writer Will Graves in Pittsburgh contributed to this story. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Reunion for Jim Harbaugh and Jesse Minter comes with both the Chargers and Ravens spiraling
stories.summary: — Jim Harbaugh and Jesse Minter won a national championship together at the college level, then led the Los Angeles Chargers to back-to-back playoff appearances.
stories.detailText: OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- — Jim Harbaugh and Jesse Minter won a national championship together at the college level, then led the Los Angeles Chargers to back-to-back playoff appearances. Now they're opponents, each in charge of his own team. And 2026 hasn't been easy for either. “I know he’s really motivated to get his team prepared. We’re really motivated to get our team prepared,” Harbaugh said. “It’ll be opposing wills meeting Monday night.” When Minter's Baltimore Ravens host Harbaugh's Los Angeles Chargers, it will be a reunion for the two coaches. Minter was Harbaugh's defensive coordinator on Michigan's title-winning staff in 2023, then followed him to the Chargers. Los Angeles won 11 games in each of the past two seasons, but then Minter left to take over the Ravens and now the Chargers are 0-8. The Ravens (4-5) haven't been much better of late. They've lost four straight and are set to start their fourth quarterback in the past four weeks. The last time these teams faced each other, in 2024, it was a matchup between Jim Harbaugh and his brother John. Now John is coaching the New York Giants , but Chargers-Ravens still includes plenty of familiarity — and two coaches who can relate to each other during a tough season. “I love Jim Harbaugh, and a lot of people in that building,” Minter said. “They’re going to work. They’re going to keep their head down. They’re going to search for improvement. They’re going to try to find things each week that they can get better at and try to get better at them. I think he’s a leader through adversity.” Baltimore has already had to put quarterbacks Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve. Rookie Joe Fagnano started last week in a Thursday night loss to Jacksonville, but the Ravens traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett in the hopes of righting the ship with another primetime game coming up. The Ravens will also have their third kicker in three weeks. Tyler Loop (groin) went on IR and was replaced by Jake Moody against the Jaguars. Then Atlanta signed Moody off Baltimore's practice squad, and the Ravens brought in Riley Patterson and Harrison Mevis as kicking options. “It means a lot. This is a great organization. The Ravens are very historic,” Patterson said. “A lot of great players have come and played through here, a lot of great kickers. So, I’m excited for the opportunity.” There have been few positives for the Chargers, but at least they still have their No. 1 quarterback. Justin Herbert took eight sacks in a loss to Houston last weekend, and he was taken out late in the game with what appeared to be an issue with his non-throwing hand, but imaging came back negative and he's expected to play against Baltimore. “He should be good to go,” Harbaugh said. Need to know Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) at Baltimore (4-5). When/where to watch: Monday, 8:15 p.m. EST, ESPN. Latest odds: Ravens by 4 1/2. Against the spread: Chargers 0-7-1; Ravens 2-7. Last week: Chargers lost to the Texans 44-22; Ravens lost to the Jaguars 33-10. Last meeting: Ravens beat the Chargers 30-23 on Nov. 25, 2024, in Inglewood, California. Series record: Ravens lead 10-6. Matchup to watch Baltimore's pass rush against the Chargers' offensive line. The Ravens have struggled to get consistent pressure — even after adding Trey Hendrickson in the offseason. But Herbert has already been sacked 31 times, and Baltimore will be ready to try to add to that total. Stats and stuff — The Chargers have turned the ball over 19 times. They have multiple turnovers in five straight games. — Los Angeles went 37 consecutive offensive drives without a touchdown before finally scoring one in the fourth quarter against Houston. — The Ravens have been outscored 84-10 in the second half over the past four games. — Baltimore has lost six of its last seven at home, with three of the defeats coming at night. — Calais Campbell of the Ravens needs two tackles for loss to become the first NFL player to reach 200 since the stat was first officially tracked in 2008. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.summary: — First-year Arizona Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur is earning his paycheck this week as he works to develop an offensive game plan with a rookie...
stories.detailText: GLENDALE, Ariz. -- — First-year Arizona Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur is earning his paycheck this week as he works to develop an offensive game plan with a rookie quarterback making his first NFL start , a banged-up offensive line and a group of little-known receivers who have combined for a grand total of eight catches this season. On the other side of the field: The Los Angeles Rams and two of the best pass rushers of this generation — Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett . “It’s fun," LaFleur said, his voice dripping with sarcasm. The Cardinals (3-6) host the Rams (5-4) on Sunday and will be starting rookie quarterback Carson Beck , a third-round draft pick out of Miami. Arizona is trying to snap a 10-game home losing streak that's lasted more than a year.
